correctness.rationale: The upper bound is realized by placing label 2 on one deleted matching pair and 0 elsewhere. For weight at most 3 there can be at most one label-2 vertex; every same-side vertex then lacks a label-2 neighbor and must be positive, which forces weight at least 4, with the n=3 boundary checked separately. At weight 4 there must be exactly two label-2 vertices and no label-1 vertices; they must lie in opposite parts, and the zero vertex paired with the opposite label-2 vertex forces the two indices to coincide. Thus the minimum is 4 and the minimum functions are exactly the n deleted-pair labelings. The inspected verifier independently exhausts all ternary labelings for n from 3 through 7 and matches both the optimum and the complete minimum-set classification; this finite check corroborates but does not replace the all-n proof.
